response: Tests in HackerRank stay active indefinitely by default. There is no automatic expiration unless you explicitly configure a Test Expiration Time with an end date. According to the documentation, the Test Expiration Time fields (start date/time and end date/time) are empty by default, meaning candidates can access the test at any time until you set an expiration. If you want to limit how long a test remains active, you can go to Settings > General and define a start and end date/time in the Test Expiration Time section. After a test expires, invited candidates cannot access it, the Invite button is disabled, and you cannot invite new candidates.

Candidates can attempt the test only during the active period. After the test expires: - Invited candidates cannot access the test. - The Invite button is disabled. - You cannot invite new candidates.' Document 5 confirms: 'Test expiration time: Define a start and end time (including time zone) for when the test remains active. Candidates can only take the test during this window.'

You should use variants when you want to personalize evaluation based on roles, skills, or other criteria within one assessment, eliminating the need to manage separate tests and reducing maintenance overhead. Create a new test (via predefined role or custom test) when you have fundamentally different hiring needs, roles, or assessment structures that are not variations of the same core evaluation.

Advantages of variants (documented):
- Single assessment adapts to multiple candidate profiles
- Eliminates managing separate tests
- Improves efficiency
- Reduces maintenance overhead
- Enables personalization at scale
- Candidates assessed on most relevant content
- Variant logic can route candidates based on qualifying questions

The documentation does not list explicit disadvantages of variants. It focuses on benefits such as streamlined management and flexibility.
